newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine term rates slip after auction decline.
newsitem.headline: Philippine term rates slip after auction decline.

text.p: Philippine term rates slipped in line with falls in Treasury bill rates at Monday's auction, traders said.
"Everybody adjusted their rates following the auction rates," one trader said.
Active secondary trading was noted especially in the longer-termed bills, with some six-month bills being dealt at 10.75 percent and one-year bills at 11.225 percent.
The secondary rates were lower than the average auction rate for the six-month bills which was at 10.887 percent, and one-year bills at 11.375 percent.
"Many banks were buying up the bills in anticipation of further dips in the coming auctions," the trader said.
Three-month bills were not traded actively since banks can still buy the Central Bank's special series bills at 10.25 percent, in line with some of the banks' offered rates.
The overnight money inched up slightly to 16.0625 percent from Monday's 16.03125 percent as some small banks entered the interbank market after their credit lines with other banks filled up.
"It's just that some banks have no other option but to access the interbank for them to cover their deficiency," one trader said, adding that the market remained generally liquid.
